title: How Rigidly Weil Positivity on a Finite Window Fixes the Weights of the Primes
content: Weil's quadratic form $\mathcal Q_a$ on $L^2(-a,a)$ depends on the primes only through the weights $w_n=\Lambda(n)n^{-1/2}$, \( a≤1.82 \), where the Weil form of the Davenport–Heilbronn function is already negative [4]. We ask how precisely positivity determines these weights. If all weights are changed by amounts whose sum is less than half the lowest point \( \lambda^*(a) \), positivity persists. In the other direction we certify in ball arithmetic, with explicit polynomial witnesses, that raising a single weight by more than $\delta_n^+$ destroys positivity, and we give certified two-sided brackets $4.9999\cdot10^{-62}\le\lambda^*(1.3)\le8.2191\cdot10^{-62}$. At $a=1.3$ the weight of $n=2$ is fixed from above to within $6.6\cdot10^{-61}$, that of $n=13$, at the edge of the window, only to within $9.4\cdot10^{-12}$. Numerically the window of admissible changes is bounded on both sides and asymmetric (for $n=2$ lowering the weight is allowed $10^5$–$3\cdot10^6$ times more than raising it; the asymmetry shrinks towards the edge of the window), and for a fixed prime power it closes very rapidly once $a$ passes $\frac12\log n$, by some 40 orders of magnitude within 0.3. We also follow the lowest point numerically as a function of $a$. A dilation (Hellmann–Feynman) formula for $d\lambda^*/da$ agrees with the slopes of the Ritz values to within 3.5% on [1.2,1.3]. Numerically, the ground state vanishes at the endpoints like $\beta(\log1/\delta)^{-1/2}$, as for the logarithmic Laplacian. At $a=0.3$ the data confirm the Hadamard-type formula $d\lambda^*/da=-2\beta^2$, which is stated with a proof in a recent preprint of Chekmachev. We show how this formula follows, conditionally, from a Pohozaev identity for the logarithmic Laplacian, with the prime terms cancelling identically. The Ritz values also obey \( -\log\lambda^*=4\pi e^{2a}-10a-15.5 \) to within 0.22 on [0.9,1.3] and, without refitting, to within 0.15 on [1.35,1.6], the scale of the prolate concentration deficit. Conditionally, positivity for all $a$ becomes a no-blow-up condition on the boundary concentration $\beta^2/\lambda^*$; this is a reformulation, not progress towards the Riemann hypothesis. This quantifies, on finite windows, the stability of the passage from the zeros to the primes. Nothing here bears on the Riemann hypothesis itself.dummy
